newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile/Japan group to build 25,000T copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Chile/Japan group to build 25,000T copper mine.

text.p: A Chilean/Japanese consortium is planning to build a copper mine in northern Chile which will produce 25,200 tonnes of fine copper a year from 1999, said the companies in a statement to the government paper Diario Oficial.
The mine will be developed by Cominor, owned by Chile's Errazuriz group, and Japanese companies Nittetsu and Itochu Corp.
A Cominor official said the Chilean firm is likely to own 60 percent of the project which will cost between $85 million and $90 million to build.
The deposit, known as El Bronce de Atacama, lies near the northern town of Copiapo in the northern Atacama Desert.
The mine, which will produce copper concentrates through the flotation process, is expected to have a useful life of 12 years, said the statement.
